h1: How much does an SEO agency actually cost in India?
metaTitle: How Much Does an SEO Agency Cost? India, 2026
metaDescription: SEO agency quotes in India run ₹15,000 to ₹5,00,000 a month. We convert five real price bands into working hours so you can see what each one buys.
answer: SEO agencies in India charge ₹15,000 to ₹5,00,000 a month. At a blended delivery cost near ₹1,200 an hour, that's roughly nine to three hundred working hours on your site. Below ₹25,000 nobody can staff four disciplines, so you're buying reports. Last Agency starts at ₹75,000, smaller sites from ₹40,000.
takeaways: Every quote is a number of hours in disguise. Divide the fee by roughly ₹1,200 and subtract about 28% for tools, overhead and margin.
**₹75,000/mo is the first band where technical, content, links and analysis can all be staffed at once.** Below it, someone is doing three jobs badly.
A price band tells you capacity, not outcome. The only thing that converts capacity into outcome is a number both sides agreed to before the work started.
Lock-in is priced into cheap retainers. A twelve-month contract at ₹20,000 is ₹2,40,000 you can't stop spending.

sections.h2: The only arithmetic that matters: fee divided by hour
body: Every SEO quote you receive is a number of working hours wearing a nicer outfit. So the fastest way to judge one is to undress it.

In India, an agency's real cost per delivered hour sits between **₹1,000 and ₹1,500**. That's not the salary rate — it's the salary loaded with PF, gratuity, a laptop, a seat, health cover, and the awkward fact that nobody bills 100% of their working day. Take ₹1,200 as the blended midpoint of a team that mixes a senior strategist with a content executive.

Then subtract the part of your fee that never reaches your account: software, admin, sales, the bench between clients, and margin. On a healthy Indian agency that's roughly 28% of the invoice. What's left, divided by ₹1,200, is how many hours anyone will actually spend on your site this month.
It's a blunt sum. It's also usually within 20% of the truth, and it will tell you more in thirty seconds than a forty-slide deck will in an hour.

callout.title: Where ₹1,200 comes from
callout.body: A specialist on ₹10,00,000 CTC costs about ₹13,00,000 fully loaded. Spread across roughly 130 genuinely billable hours a month, that's ₹833 an hour. A lead on ₹20,00,000 lands nearer ₹1,700. Blend a real team and you land between ₹1,000 and ₹1,500.

sections.h2: Five price bands, and the hours each one funds
body: Here are the five bands Indian agency quotes actually cluster around, converted into delivered hours. Ex-GST throughout, because almost every quote you'll see is quoted ex-GST and then arrives 18% heavier.

One competent generalist for about a day a week. Viable for a local site under 30 pages.
A strategist, a technical specialist, a writer and an outreach exec sharing your account. First band where four disciplines coexist.
Same team, real content cadence, a funded link programme. National keyword sets, ecommerce, SaaS.
A dedicated pod. Multiple markets or languages, migrations, in-house coordination, a developer you can call.

bullets: **Under ₹25,000 a month, no version of this funds four disciplines.** Nine to eighteen hours buys a report and some on-page edits. That's not fraud, it's arithmetic — the problem is the pitch deck rarely says so out loud. We took that apart in [the lowest price of SEO](/cost/lowest-price-of-seo).

**₹40,000 to ₹75,000 buys more than 1.9x the hours — it buys different people.** Below ₹40,000, one generalist eventually does something badly. Above it you can afford someone who has personally recovered a site from a botched migration, which is a very specific and very expensive kind of experience.

**Past ₹1,50,000, coordination starts eating the increase.** More people means more handoffs. The marginal rupee at ₹3,00,000 does less work than the marginal rupee at ₹75,000, and any agency that tells you otherwise has a sales target.

sections.h2: What actually changes as the number goes up
body: The bands aren't just more of the same thing. Each one changes what's possible, and the change isn't linear.

At this level, spreading the budget across technical, content and links guarantees all three stay stuck. Pick the one binding constraint and spend everything there. Usually it's either the site being unindexable or there being no pages worth indexing.
A good freelancer often beats a cheap agency here, because you're paying for one person's attention either way and the freelancer doesn't have an office to fund.

Around 24 to 45 delivered hours. Enough for two to four researched articles a month, ongoing technical hygiene, and someone actually reading Search Console. Enough for a 20-to-60-page services site in a competitive city.
Not enough for meaningful link acquisition. Earned links cost hours, not fees, and hours are exactly what's scarce here.
This is where the work stops being sequential. Technical fixes ship while content is being written while outreach is running. The compounding starts because nothing is waiting for anything else.
It's also where the agency can afford to be wrong occasionally — to test a content format, kill it, and try another — which is how anything good gets found.

subs.h3: ₹1,50,000 and above — scale, and the cost of coordinating it
body: Multiple languages, tens of thousands of SKUs, replatforming, or three markets at once. Real work, genuinely expensive.
Ask what proportion of the fee goes to project management. If it's over 20%, you're buying a process, not an outcome.

sections.h2: What we charge, and who carries the risk
body: Our numbers, in full, so you can hold them against the table above.

SEO runs **from ₹75,000/mo**, with smaller sites from **₹40,000/mo**. Organic Social & Content is ₹30,000, ₹50,000 or ₹70,000 a month. Performance Marketing is ₹40,000, ₹75,000 or ₹1,50,000 a month. Bundled: SEO plus social is ₹99,000/mo, social plus performance is ₹75,000/mo, all three is ₹1,75,000/mo. All ex-GST. Ad spend is billed separately with zero media markup.
The part that changes the arithmetic isn't the price, though. It's what happens if the price doesn't work.

On day one we freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search. That number goes in writing before anyone touches the site. If we haven't beaten it in 90 days, we keep working free until we do. We never promise a specific ranking position for a specific keyword — nobody controls Google's index, and anyone who says otherwise is selling you a coin flip. We promise movement against **your own** baseline, which is the only number that pays your salaries.
That's also why we only take three new clients a month. You cannot carry that risk at volume, and agencies that pretend they can are quietly relying on you not measuring.

callout.title: The question a price alone can't answer
callout.body: Two agencies quote ₹75,000. One will invoice you in month four regardless. One won't. Same number, completely different product. Ask which one you're buying before you compare the rupees.

sections.h2: Five questions to ask a quote before you sign
body: Ask these in the meeting, not over email. You're measuring how long the pause is.
numbered: **"How many hours a month does this fee fund, and split by role?"** An agency that has planned the work answers in ten seconds. One that hasn't will tell you they don't work in hours, which is a real philosophy and also a very convenient one.
**"What number are we measuring, and what is it today?"** If nobody writes down the starting point, nobody can prove movement later. This is the question that most often ends a sales call early.
**"Who specifically does the work, and are they in this room?"** The pitch team and the delivery team are frequently different people. That's normal. Not telling you is not.

**"Where do the links come from?"** "Our network" means a private blog network. "We buy from vendors" means the same links your competitor bought. Both are penalties with a delay fuse. See [what link building actually costs](/cost/link-building-cost).
**"What happens if this doesn't work?"** Listen for whether the answer contains a consequence for them or only a plan for you.

sections.h2: The notice period is part of the price
body: A ₹20,000/mo retainer on a twelve-month lock-in is not ₹20,000. It's ₹2,40,000 you have already committed to spending, and you will find that out in month five when nothing has moved and the exit clause requires 90 days' notice.

Long contracts exist because SEO takes time — that argument is genuinely true. They also exist because they protect agency revenue from agency underperformance, and that argument is genuinely true too. The honest version is a short commitment plus a reason to stay.

We run month-to-month after the first quarter, 30 days' notice, and you keep every asset — content, links, dashboards, documentation — whatever happens. Switching agencies is expensive enough without your last one holding your Search Console access hostage.

If you want the full ladder by city and site size, [what SEO costs in India](/cost/seo-cost-in-india) breaks the same numbers down by headcount, and [our pricing page](/pricing) has the current rate card.

faqs.q: What is a reasonable monthly SEO budget in India?
faqs.a: For a small local site, ₹40,000 a month is a genuine starting line. For a competitive national keyword set, ₹75,000 to ₹1,50,000. Below ₹25,000 you're funding under 20 delivered hours, which covers reporting and small edits but nothing structural.

faqs.q: Why do SEO agency quotes for the same site vary so much?
faqs.a: Because they're quoting different amounts of work and rarely saying so. One quote may include four researched articles, technical fixes and outreach; another may include a monthly report and title tag edits. Ask both for an hours-by-role split and the gap usually explains itself.

faqs.q: Is GST included in SEO agency pricing?
faqs.a: Usually not. Almost every Indian agency quotes ex-GST, then adds 18% on the invoice. A ₹75,000 retainer bills at ₹88,500. If your business is GST-registered you can claim that as input credit, so it's a cash-flow cost rather than a real one — but budget for it.

faqs.q: Should I pay an SEO agency hourly or monthly?
faqs.a: Monthly, once you need more than about 30 hours a month, which nearly every site past 50 pages does. Hourly makes sense for a defined diagnostic or a second opinion. It's a poor fit for work that compounds, because it prices attention rather than continuity.

faqs.q: Can an SEO agency guarantee results?
faqs.a: Not a ranking position — nobody controls Google's index. What an agency can honestly guarantee is movement against a baseline you both agree on and freeze before work starts. Ours is your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic search; miss it in 90 days and we work free until we beat it.

faqs.q: How long before an SEO agency is worth what I'm paying?
faqs.a: Leading indicators — impressions and average position on your target queries — should move inside four to eight weeks. Real movement on a competitive set takes three to six months, and compounding returns six to twelve. Flat impressions at month three is a conversation worth having immediately.
